name: Eugene F. Kranz Toledo Express Airport
before:
Toledo's airport, ten miles west of the city in western Lucas County, and a joint civil and military field. The Ohio Air National Guard's 180th Fighter Wing is based here.

Its role is shaped by Detroit. Toledo Express works as a secondary airport for the region and is the primary diversion point when Detroit Metropolitan cannot take aircraft. That same proximity hollowed out its scheduled service: seven airlines and more than 40 flights a day in the 1990s had fallen to two airlines by 2011 as passengers drove to Detroit instead.

It has recovered since. Traffic bottomed out in 2012 and grew for six straight years to 241,299 passengers in 2018, helped by a growing Charlotte service.

There is an eight gate domestic terminal on the north side and an 81 acre cargo ramp on the south. Two runways serve the 2,345 acre site, the longer at 10,600 feet. The Ohio Turnpike is at exit 52.

The airport was renamed in September 2020 after Gene Kranz, the NASA flight director and Toledo native.
after:
Toledo's airport, west of the city in Lucas County. It is a joint civil and military field: the Ohio Air National Guard's 180th Fighter Wing is based here.

Its scheduled service is small. Allegiant is now the only passenger airline, flying mainly to Florida: Orlando Sanford, Punta Gorda, St Pete-Clearwater and Sarasota. The FAA counted about 67,000 passengers boarding here in 2025. For anywhere else, look at Detroit Metropolitan, a major hub.

Cargo is handled on a ramp on the south side. Two runways serve the 2,345 acre site, the longer at 10,600 feet. Drivers reach it from exit 52 of the Ohio Turnpike.

The airport was renamed in 2020 after Gene Kranz, the NASA flight director and Toledo native.

claims.note: New, replacing the Charlotte service. The Port Authority and the operator's page call Sarasota seasonal and also list a seasonal Phoenix-Mesa route, but BTS shows no Phoenix-Mesa passengers in the twelve months to June 2026, so Phoenix is left out and 'seasonal' (one organisation) is not stated. Review, 23 Sep: 'mainly' added because the operator's live airlines page (re-fetched as recheck-airlines) still advertises 'NONSTOP TO PHOENIX/MESA, ARIZONA (AZA) - SEASONAL'. Phoenix-Mesa itself has only the operator behind it, so it is not named, but 'flying to Florida' alone would read as the whole network.

claims.claim: FAA: about 67,000 passengers boarded here in 2025
claims.inAfter: The FAA counted about 67,000 passengers boarding here in 2025.
claims.note: ENPLANEMENTS (boardings only), attributed to the FAA, whose own table is the source: 66,949 in CY2025, up 0.50 per cent, in the FAA's non-hub class. No operator total for 2025 was found. BTS, whose data the FAA's counts draw on, gives 67,000 scheduled departing passengers in the twelve months to June 2026. Replaces the 2018 figure of 241,299 passengers (arrivals plus departures), which the old text used to say traffic had recovered; the airport's boardings are now roughly half that 2018 level, on the FAA's count.

claims.why: Fails the coordinates check: 22.7 km (14.1 miles) from the centre of Toledo in a straight line, a ratio of 0.71. The FAA's master record gives 10 nautical miles (11.5 statute miles). The sources disagree, so the figure is dropped and the direction kept.

claims.claim: its role is shaped by Detroit
claims.wasBefore: Its role is shaped by Detroit.
claims.why: The lead-in to a paragraph that rests on Wikipedia alone (below). The practical point, that clients going anywhere but Florida will look at Detroit, is kept as advice.

claims.claim: secondary airport and primary diversion point for Detroit
claims.wasBefore: Toledo Express works as a secondary airport for the region and is the primary diversion point when Detroit Metropolitan cannot take aircraft
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Neither the operator's pages nor the Port Authority's 2025 annual report say so, and the Wayne County Airport Authority's 2017 master plan for Detroit lists Toledo Express only as a nearby airport and a possible home for cargo operators.

claims.claim: recovered since, 241,299 passengers in 2018, growing Charlotte service
claims.wasBefore: It has recovered since. Traffic bottomed out in 2012 and grew for six straight years to 241,299 passengers in 2018, helped by a growing Charlotte service.

The Charlotte service has gone (BTS: Allegiant 100 per cent, no Charlotte among the destinations; the operator lists Charlotte only as a route request), and the FAA counted 66,949 boardings in 2025, roughly half the 2018 level. The 2018 figure itself rests on Wikipedia alone.
